conflicts.claim: Glomerulosa may lack the full enzyme suite for autonomous aldosterone synthesis (zonal cooperation proposed).
conflicts.note: Vinson 2016 (largely rodent data) challenges strict zonal autonomy; the textbook model (Guyton & Hall) assigns aldosterone synthesis to the zona glomerulosa. Both kept; V1 viewer follows the textbook model.

quantity.measure: Basal plasma AVP, healthy hydrated adult men (immunoassay)
quantity.notes: Baylis 1986: immunoreactive AVP 1.3 ± 0.3 pmol/L (mean ± SEM, n = 8). Converted with M = 1084.25 g/mol (ChEBI CHEBI:34543): 1.41 pg/mL. Range = mean ± 2 SEM. Assay-dependent: see conflicts.

conflicts.claim: Cytochemical bioassay in the same subjects gave 0.96 ± 0.14 pmol/L (≈1.04 pg/mL).
conflicts.note: Same study, different assay; both kept.

conflicts.claim: Regression y = 0.35(x − 281.0) predicts ≈2.1 pg/mL at a plasma osmolality of 287 mOsm/kg.
conflicts.note: Different cohort and assay; the engine state ADH (typical 1–3 pg/mL) spans both.

relations.notes: Phosphorylation-dependent translocation of AQP2 from storage vesicles to the apical membrane; reversible on AVP withdrawal (Nielsen 1995, rat).

quantity.measure: Vasopressin-stimulated (50 pM) osmotic water permeability Pf of isolated perfused rat inner medullary collecting duct
quantity.notes: Three series in Wang 2020: 146 ± 16 (female, N=3), 92 ± 14 (male, N=3), 55 ± 10 µm/s (N=4); value = median of series means, range = span of series means. Rat, in vitro; the human value and the fold-change versus no AVP are NOT established here (V2 gap).

conflicts.claim: Vasopressin-independent Pf of about 300 µm/s in IMCDs from 24-h water-deprived rats.
conflicts.note: Higher than the AVP-stimulated values above; differs in animal hydration state (dehydrated donors) and laboratory. Not reconciled.

conflicts.claim: Transcellular Posm 36.0 ± 2.4 µm/s with AVP in thirsted-rat IMCDs.
conflicts.note: Expressed per unit basolateral membrane area corrected for infoldings, so not on the same area basis as luminal Pf; not directly comparable.

relations.notes: Net effect: increases collecting-duct water permeability and water reabsorption (antidiuresis).
Magnocellular neurons are themselves intrinsically osmosensitive (rodent cellular data).

quantity.measure: Slope of plasma AVP vs plasma osmolality above threshold
quantity.notes: Mirrors engine parameter adh_slope. Threshold (x-intercept) is engine adh_threshold = 281.0 [278.0, 285.5] mOsm/kg.

conflicts.claim: Osmotic threshold 281.0 mOsm/kg recumbent; 277.8 upright; 282 during hypertonic saline.

conflicts.note: Different cohort and protocol (hypertonic saline infusion). Inside the engine range [278.0, 285.5].
Systematic-review pooled value; higher than Robertson & Athar recumbent 281.0. Inside the engine range.

conflicts.claim: Curvilinear AVP-osmolality relation that "militated against the concept of an osmotic threshold".
conflicts.note: Structural disagreement with the threshold-linear model used by the engine; kept visible.

quantity.measure: Plasma osmolality at which thirst begins
quantity.notes: Mirrors engine parameter thirst_threshold (systematic review pooled value).

conflicts.claim: Thirst threshold 281 mOsm/kg, similar to the AVP threshold.
conflicts.note: Single study; at the lower bound of the engine range [281, 287].

conflicts.claim: Common teaching that the thirst threshold lies several mOsm/kg above the AVP threshold.
conflicts.note: Not supported by these sources, which find the thresholds similar. Teaching claim is not itself cited here because no verified source for it was located.

quantity.measure: Plasma half-life of AVP

conflicts.note: Unsourced brief value; the verified primary value (24.1 min mean, n = 10) is used. Recorded for traceability.

relations.notes: High distal NaCl delivery sensed at the macula densa suppresses renin release (low delivery stimulates it).
Edge target is the substrate; product is angiotensin I (see rel:raas:agt-to-angi).
Renin-catalysed cleavage.
ACE-catalysed conversion.
Edge target is the product here (aldosterone synthase final steps).

conflicts.claim: Zona glomerulosa may not synthesise aldosterone autonomously.

quantity.measure: Engine sensitivity of aldosterone target to ECF volume (dimensionless exponent)
quantity.notes: Mirrors engine parameter; lumps the whole RAAS into one volume-sensing gain. E-assumption: surfaced in the UI.

relations.notes: Ligand-bound MR acts in the nucleus.

quantity.measure: Engine exponent of aldosterone effect on fractional Na excretion
quantity.notes: Mirrors engine parameter. E-assumption: surfaced in the UI.

quantity.measure: Engine exponent of ANP effect on fractional Na excretion

conflicts.claim: Plasma ANP did not change during salt-load natriuresis in healthy humans.
conflicts.note: Contrasts with the classical natriuretic role of ANP (Potter 2006; Kuhn 2016). Both kept; the engine uses a weak ANP effect.

quantity.measure: Plasma half-life of ANP
Pump stoichiometry (Na+)
quantity.notes: Textbook 3 Na+ out : 2 K+ in per cycle. Post & Jolly 1957 is the historical origin; its full text was not reviewed, so the grade rests on the textbook. Fixed stoichiometry (degenerate range by definition).

quantity.measure: Pump stoichiometry (K+)

relations.notes: Basolateral pumping sets the gradient for apical Na entry in every reabsorbing segment.

quantity.measure: Glomerular filtration rate, adult population (US NHANES 1999–2006, CKD-EPI estimate)
quantity.notes: Median and IQR of estimated (not measured) GFR in the general adult population, all ages. Values are body-surface-area normalised.

conflicts.claim: Textbook GFR about 125 mL/min (180 L/day) in a young adult (not BSA-normalised); engine GFR_0 = 125 [100, 140] mL/min.
conflicts.note: Different population (young reference adult vs whole population), measurement (classic clearance vs creatinine estimate) and normalisation. For a 70 kg adult with BSA about 1.8–1.9 m², 125 mL/min ≈ 115–120 mL/min/1.73 m².

conflicts.claim: Median eGFR 85 (men) and 83 (women) mL/min/1.73 m² at age 30–34 in healthy Dutch adults; decline ≈0.4 mL/min/year.
conflicts.note: MDRD equation, which underestimates at higher GFR (Levey 2009).
Conventional teaching range; no verified source for it located in this pass (KDIGO 2024 metadata verified but its G1 ≥90 threshold could not be read in an accessible text). Not used.

relations.notes: Slit diaphragm restricts passage of macromolecules (selective permeability), not water flux per se.

quantity.unit: fraction of filtered Na load reabsorbed
quantity.measure: Segmental fractional Na reabsorption, proximal tubule
quantity.notes: Textbook point value (Guyton & Hall 2021; chapter/page not verified by this agent). Range is a curator assumption of about ±5 percentage points around the textbook value. Palmer & Schnermann 2015 supports the qualitative division of labour; its percentages were not accessible. Point value 0.66 chosen inside the textbook 65–70% so the four segment point values sum to 0.99 (fractional excretion ≈1%, consistent with >99% total reabsorption).

quantity.unit: fraction of filtered Na load reabsorbed
quantity.measure: Segmental fractional Na reabsorption, loop of Henle (thick ascending limb)
quantity.notes: Textbook point value (Guyton & Hall 2021; chapter/page not verified by this agent). Range is a curator assumption of about ±5 percentage points around the textbook value. Palmer & Schnermann 2015 supports the qualitative division of labour; its percentages were not accessible.

quantity.unit: fraction of filtered Na load reabsorbed
quantity.measure: Segmental fractional Na reabsorption, distal convoluted tubule
quantity.notes: Textbook point value (Guyton & Hall 2021; chapter/page not verified by this agent). Range is a curator assumption of about ±5 percentage points around the textbook value. Palmer & Schnermann 2015 supports the qualitative division of labour; its percentages were not accessible. Palmer & Schnermann: the DCT vs downstream split is variable and coupled to K balance.

quantity.unit: fraction of filtered Na load reabsorbed
quantity.measure: Segmental fractional Na reabsorption, connecting tubule + collecting duct (aldosterone-regulated)
quantity.notes: Textbook point value (Guyton & Hall 2021; chapter/page not verified by this agent). Range is a curator assumption of about ±5 percentage points around the textbook value. Palmer & Schnermann 2015 supports the qualitative division of labour; its percentages were not accessible.

quantity.measure: Engine gain of pressure natriuresis on fractional Na excretion
quantity.notes: Mirrors engine parameter. Mechanism (proximal) per Ivy & Bailey 2014. E-assumption: surfaced in the UI.

relations.notes: Arterial (renal perfusion) pressure is the input to pressure natriuresis.

quantity.measure: Half-time of absorption of ingested plain water
Half-time of intestinal absorption of ingested sodium

relations.notes: 2026-10-03 (health-literature-curator, tracker W-6): ev:suckling-2012 added for direction only. Plasma sodium rose after salted versus unsalted soup, so ingested sodium reached plasma; no number is taken (its dispersion is SEM/SD unverified) and the quantity's evidence and grade are unchanged.
